Understanding Tide Pools

Tide pools are rocky depressions along the shore that hold seawater when the tide goes out. They host a surprising diversity of life, from anemones and sea stars to tiny crabs that shelter beneath stones.

Zones of the shore

Ecologists divide the rocky shore into several zones. Each zone is exposed to air for a different share of the day, and the organisms living there are adapted to that rhythm of exposure and submersion.

  • The spray zone is wetted only by waves.
  • The high intertidal zone is submerged at high tide.
  • The low intertidal zone is exposed only during the lowest tides.

Researchers log temperatures with small waterproof sensors. The analysis script below converts raw readings into daily maxima, which makes it easy to compare zones across seasons and years.

def daily_max(readings):
    return max(readings)

Every tide pool is a world in miniature.
